title: Open restriction of pro-etale direct image with counit normalization
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $h:W\hookrightarrow Y$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $X_W=X\times_YW$, with projections $g:X_W\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_W:X_W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the actual inverse images and direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], coefficient rings $R_X=f^{-1}R$, $R_W=h^{-1}R$ and $R_{X_W}=g^{-1}R_X\cong f_W^{-1}R_W$, and the module adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f_W^{-1}\dashv f_{W,*}$ for these inverse-image coefficient rings [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. For every $R_X$-module sheaf $M$ on $X$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\beta_M:h^{-1}f_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{W,*}g^{-1}M.$$
Under the open-slice identifications [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison], its evaluation at $E\to W$ is the fibre-product identification $M(X\times_YE)\cong M(X_W\times_WE)$. It is compatible with the specified adjunction counits: writing $\alpha_F:g^{-1}f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_W^{-1}h^{-1}F$ for the canonical inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], one has
$$g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,M})=\varepsilon_{f_W,g^{-1}M}\circ f_W^{-1}(\beta_M)\circ\alpha_{f_*M}.$$
No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, properness, closed-immersion, constant-ring or finiteness assumption is imposed on $f$ or $R$.

proof.text: Compare the canonical ring-module inverse image along a weakly etale map h with direct restriction along objectComposition h. The site adjunction mapPullbackAdj induces a sheaf adjunction. Its left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism identifies h inverse R with the restriction of R; the unit-conjugacy equation gives both coefficient triangle identities. Apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj with these coefficient maps, and compare its left adjoint with proEtaleRingModuleAdjunction by leftAdjointUniq. The hom-equivalence equation identifies its evaluation with objectCoprojection, hence that coprojection is bijective for every object. This applies to h and the first pullback projection, since an open immersion and its base change are weakly etale.

Construct the projection-preserving squareSiteIso by the fibre-product composition comparisons. Its ring mate is ringSquareIso, and coefficientIso is its inverse evaluated on R. The conjugate unit equation shows that the coefficient maps for the two composite module pushforwards agree under squareSiteIso. Compose Mathlib pushforwardComp and pushforwardCongr₂ to compare these right adjoints. Take the inverse conjugate isomorphism of their composite canonical adjunctions to obtain alpha. Evaluating unit_conjugateEquiv_symm on a section proves exactly AlphaNormalization.

Define betaMate as the mate of alpha inverse under the f and second-projection module adjunctions. Mathlib mateEquiv_counit and alpha hom-inverse cancellation prove the CounitEquation for this natural transformation. AlphaNormalization, naturality and the f-adjunction right triangle compute betaMate on unit sections: it is the first-projection unit followed by restriction along squareSiteIso inverse.

Apply naturality to the distinguished object units in objectCoprojection. The equality K.map(unit_h) followed by squareSiteIso inverse equals unit_g followed by G.map(sectionArrow) follows from pullback.hom_ext, expanding pullbackComp and pullbackCongr and checking their projections. Together with the preceding unit-section computation and naturality of the g unit, this gives the required sectionwise formula for betaMate. Construct an inverse to sectionArrow by two pullback lifts; both composites are identities by pullback.hom_ext. Its action on sections is thus bijective. Since both object coprojections are bijective by step 1, the formula implies every section component of betaMate is bijective. Module-sheaf forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms, so these components give the natural isomorphism beta. Assemble beta, its section formula, alpha, its normalization and the already proved mate counit equation.
